summary: Ran a 22-case matrix against the patched copy and the pristine snapshot. Entity-hidden schemes were removed from link, image source, video poster, form action, blockquote cite, generic background and SVG link attributes. All allowed, relative, query-ampersand, custom-protocol, entity-encoded-http, non-ASCII-prefix, unknown-entity and double-encoded controls were byte-identical before and after, and no case raised an exception. The comparison found one remaining policy gap: a decimal numeric reference without a trailing semicolon was not decoded by the helper. The serializer escaped its ampersand, so re-parsing the pristine output yielded a relative-looking value rather than a script scheme, but the policy still failed to see the resolved prefix. Evidence strength: direct multi-attribute matrix with byte controls. Limitation: the no-semicolon form needed a separate parser-semantics check.
next_hint: Decide whether the policy decoder should consume numeric digit runs without a trailing semicolon, matching HTML tokenizer termination, and keep invalid numeric references unchanged so malformed controls do not drift.
